# Architecture — Perry > Written by: agent · Confirmed by: user (§1, §3 Forbidden, §5 versions, §6, §7) > Version: v1 > Last reviewed: 2026-09-15 > Hard cap: ≤ 500 lines. It has two readers — the user in one sitting, and every > agent that is dispatched against it — and the second one pays for it per turn. > Overflow → split per-§ to `architecture/sections/§-.md`. **This file existing is what makes it binding.** There is no draft state: a document that describes the system is the description, and a change that contradicts a section stops and asks the user (DESIGN-017 decisions 2 and 4). ## §1. Mission & scope Perry is a project office for solo and small projects, run by agents and read by one human. It keeps goals, work and decisions as files in the project's own repository, and it computes every number it reports rather than eyeballing it. It runs as a **skill** on three hosts — Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex CLI — with no install step and no service. The `bin/` tools are stdlib-only Python 3 and POSIX-ish bash, invoked by the skill's own procedures. It deliberately does **not**: run unattended (every write is a command an agent was asked to make), judge what a document means in code (that is an agent's job, `DESIGN-014`), or hold state outside the project it is pointed at (`ADR-002` — there is no cross-project registry). ## §2. Components ### `bin/` — the deterministic tools - **Purpose**: read and write project state. Twenty-one executables plus three shared libraries; `perry-kernel` is the `kernel/` CLI below. - **Owns**: every write to a canonical store, every computed number the standup prints, the argument contract those calls are made through, and the **next-step recommendation**: `perry-state --section next` evaluates the declared rule table `reference/next-rules.json` over the payload it already computes, so the same state gives the same recommendation. The move is the user's decision, `perry/design/DESIGN-020-guided-planning.md § 9`, the 2026-09-15 entry, confirmed by the user in session. - **Doesn't own**: the rules, which are declared in `reference/`, or the procedure around a recommendation — when to show it and what to ask the user are the `SKILL.md` files'. These tools execute, compute and refuse. - **Module document**: [`bin/ARCHITECTURE.md`](bin/ARCHITECTURE.md) ### `kernel/` — the PMO kernel (DESIGN-023) - **Purpose**: hold a project's structured state in one store per project anchor and answer for it through one CLI, JSON in and JSON out. Built by DESIGN-023 § 6 row B, behind `bin/perry-kernel`; `bin/` stays the live writer until each lane cuts over. - **Owns**: the store (`/perry/.db`, or `/.perry/perry.db` outside git) and its deterministic export under `/export/`; eight concepts and at most twelve command groups; every structural check a guard can decide without reading for meaning; and the derived fields `startable`, `blocked_by`, a metric's `met` and `fraction`, and `rollup`. - **Doesn't own**: the method. Item types, states, fields and guards are the process template, which the skill ships as data under `templates/process/`. The kernel reads no markdown, runs no command, and names no skill path or template-declared name. - **Module document**: [`kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md`](kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md) ### `release/` — Perry product versions and releases - **Purpose**: maintain Perry's own product versions and verified release updates. - **Owns**: typed release records, deterministic VERSION/CHANGELOG projections, integration checks and explicit publication of an exact tested commit. - **Doesn't own**: the versions or state of projects managed by Perry, the meaning of authored change notes, or the user's decision to raise a major version. - **Procedure**: [`release/README.md`](release/README.md). ### `viewer/parsers.py` — the one reader - **Purpose**: parse every state file. 5,228 lines, one implementation. - **Owns**: `OKR.md`, phase, linkage, config and architecture parsing, and the store readers the read payloads answer from — a `BOARD.md` a project still holds is parsed only for the import verbs (TASK-262 round 4b); the project-root and state-root resolution, and the `installed` predicate, both `bin/` and the skill read through. - **Doesn't own**: writing. A second parser is the defect this repository has shipped twice; `NN-1` below is that rule. ### `schema/` — the declared shape - **Purpose**: `state-schema.json` (107KB) declares every file, heading, table, enum, store and claim. Eight contract pages publish the payloads outside consumers read; `next-contract.md` is the eighth. - **Owns**: what a file must look like, and what a payload promises. - **Doesn't own**: how a tool reaches that shape. ### `SKILL.md` + `goals/` `work/` `decide/` — the lanes - **Purpose**: the router (tier 0, read on every invocation; its byte cap is `tests/test_router_budget.py`'s) and three lane files loaded on demand. - **Owns**: procedure — what an agent does, in what order, and when it stops to ask the user. A lane **renders** the next step `perry-state --section next` returns: **in a standup's TL;DR and in its next-step position** it does not add, drop or reorder a recommendation, and it may add one line marked as its own note (`perry/design/DESIGN-020-guided-planning.md § 9`, the 2026-09-15 entry, confirmed by the user in session). - **Outside that rule**, and still the lane's own to write: a procedural step inside a subcommand's instructions ("read this, then run that"); the remediation a refusal names ("no current phase — run `plan-phase` first"); bootstrap and first-run prompts; and a hint in a rendered dashboard row. First-time setup is the largest of them: on a directory with no Perry state `R-setup` recommends only `/perry`, and the order setup recommends after that is the router's own (`reference/first-run.md § The recommended order for a new project`, which the router's first-time setup points to). The rule is about the one position the next block owns, not about naming a command. - **Doesn't own**: any number, or which step to recommend. Every figure a lane prints comes from a `bin/` call, and so does the recommendation. ### `modes/`, `packs/`, `reference/`, `templates/` - **Purpose**: the domain pack (`software-ops`), tier-1 reference pages loaded on demand, document scaffolds, and `templates/process/` JSON applied through the kernel. The legacy mode pages remain until final disposal; the work lane no longer runs stage, WIP, SLA or cadence procedures. `reference/` also holds `next-rules.json`, the rule table `bin/perry-state` evaluates for the next step, and `next.md`, which explains each rule. - **Owns**: process template data, retained legacy mode vocabulary, pack glossaries and legacy next-step rules, declared as data that `bin/` evaluates. ### `tests/` — 166 modules - **Purpose**: the contract, executable. Includes `tests/tree_guard.py`, which fails the suite if a run changed the checkout it ran in. - **Owns**: whether a claim in this repository is true. ### `perry/` and `.perry/` — this project's own state - **Purpose**: Perry's state root and anchor. Perry runs its own office in its own repository. ## §3. Boundaries & dependencies ```mermaid flowchart TD User([the one human]) -->|reads, decides| Lanes Lanes["SKILL.md · goals / work / decide
procedure only"] -->|invokes| Bin Bin["bin/ — 23 tools
compute and write"] -->|imports| Parsers["viewer/parsers.py
the one reader"] Bin -->|imports| Lib["bin/lib · perry_store · perry_md_store"] Bin -->|validates against| Schema["schema/state-schema.json"] Parsers -->|reads| State[("perry/ · .perry/
stores and projections")] Bin -->|writes| State Tests["tests/ — 166 modules"] -.asserts.-> Bin Tests -.asserts.-> Parsers Tests -.asserts.-> Schema Outside([aiMark and other consumers]) -->|published payloads| Contracts["schema/*-contract.md"] Contracts -.described by.-> Bin ``` Allowed directions: lanes → tools → libraries → state. Tools import `parsers`; `parsers` imports nothing from `bin/`. Forbidden, and each one has cost this project something: - **A second reader of any state file.** `bin/` never re-implements a parse. - **A lane computing a number.** If a figure is not in a payload, the tool grows the field; the procedure does not count rows. - **A tool reaching another project.** Roots come from `--root`, then `$PERRY_PROJECT`, then the walk up — `ADR-002`, and `bin/lib § resolve_project_root` is the one implementation. **Sunset (proposed, DESIGN-023)**: this becomes false at DESIGN-023 § 6 row H. The kernel's resolver (`kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 5.7, NN-K5) is the second implementation DESIGN-023 introduces. It walks in the same order as `bin/lib § resolve_project_root` with a different predicate — it stops at the first `.perry/`, not the first installed project — and it refuses (`anchor_not_found`) where `bin/lib` falls back to the working directory or takes a `--root` or `$PERRY_PROJECT` that holds no `.perry/`. `kernel/tests/test_resolver_agreement.py` pins those four differences on both sides and shows the two agree on a shared set of fixture roots. The copies that already exist are unchanged and go at row H: `bin/perry-state § resolve_root`, `viewer/parsers.py § _resolve_project_root`, the flag/env/cwd lines in `perry-decide`, `perry-task`, `perry-knowledge`, `perry-state-cost`, `perry-explain`, `bin/perry-churn § detect_perry`, which walks up to the first `.perry/`, stops at the git top level, and takes no `--root` and no environment variable, and `perry-lint`, which reads no `$PERRY_PROJECT` at any of its nine sites: one, the default lint, walks, and eight per-mode branches (`--claims`, `--verification`, `--summaries`, `--glossary`, `--reviews`, `--knowledge`, `--provenance`, `--specs`) take `--root` or else the cwd, with no walk. - **An agent writing `ARCHITECTURE.md`.** This file is the user's. ## §4. Data flow **Current work flow:** work and aiMark call `perry-kernel`; SQLite items/events are state/history, with JSONL recovery exports. Goals/decide and the root dashboard migrate later (DESIGN-023 F/G). **Historical legacy flow below** (work writes are frozen at phase E): every mutating command writes the record first. The board is not a file: `perry-tasks board` prints it from the stores. A `BOARD.md` a project still holds is retired — no write or reader uses it, only the `--from-board` imports read it, and every tool that sees it says to import and then delete it (TASK-262 rounds 4a and 4b). ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph write["a mutating command"] direction TB A["perry-task <verb>"] --> B["tasks.jsonl
the record"] B --> C["journal/<YYYY-MM>/<day>.md
the history line"] B --> E[".perry/events.jsonl
derived, disposable"] end B -.->|"(1) and (2) are one
recoverable transaction"| C C -.->|"(3) may fail alone
— reported, not silent"| E ``` Eight stores exist, one verdict line each in `perry-lint`'s census: `tasks.jsonl`, `risks.jsonl`, `intake.jsonl`, `asks.jsonl`, `cadence.jsonl`, `okr.jsonl`, `linkage.jsonl`, `.perry/config.jsonl`. `cadence.jsonl` is the newest (TASK-237 deliverable 3b). The historical read path below remains for the legacy dashboard; current work and aiMark query the kernel: ```mermaid flowchart LR State[("stores + projections")] --> P["viewer/parsers.py"] P --> S["perry-state"] S -->|"--compact ≈ 11KB"| Standup["the standup, every session"] S -->|"--section <name>"| Detail["one key, in full"] S -->|"--section next --lane / --after"| Next["the next block,
narrowed"] S -->|"--json ≈ 174KB"| Whole["the whole payload"] T["perry-task list --json"] -->|"contract 2.4, bounded"| Outside([aiMark]) ``` `--section next` is the one section that is not always the payload's key as it stands. With `--lane` or `--after` it prints the block evaluated again over only that lane's or that subcommand's rules, plus the overlays (TASK-442). ## §5. Contracts ### Contract: `bin/` → an agent (the argument surface) - **Input**: ` [flags]`. Each tool declares its surface in `SURFACE`; the parser is driven by that declaration. - **Output**: exit 0 read or written · 1 refused, reason printed · 2 bad invocation · 3 the bytes match and the store did not produce them. These two bullets describe the other `bin/` tools: `bin/perry-kernel` has no `SURFACE` (`describe` is its surface), and its exit 3 is an internal fault (`kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 5.1). - **Invariant on the tool**: a flag reaches only the subcommands that declare it. Accepted-and-dropped is a defect (`DESIGN-016` goal 12). - **Invariant on the caller**: a refusal is an outcome, not a failure. Do not fall back to editing the file by hand. ### Contract: `perry-task list --json` → outside consumers - `schema/task-list-contract.md`, version **2.4** (confirmed by the user 2026-09-15; 2.2 adds `installed`, 2.3 narrows it to a store with `.perry/` beside it, 2.4 reads no `BOARD.md` a project still holds — TASK-262 round 4b). `tasks[]` is bounded at 200 rows by default; `bound.open_total` carries the project's figure. - **Error mode**: a refusal is JSON on stdout, not prose on stderr. ### Contract: `perry-state --json` / `--compact` → the standup - `--compact` is a strict projection of `--json`, declared once in `perry-state § COMPACT` and asserted against the full payload by test. ### Contract: the schema → both sides - `perry-lint --templates` fails when a shipped template drifts from `state-schema.json`. That check is what keeps the standup from breaking silently. ## §6. Non-negotiables ### NN-1 — One reader per state file - **Severity**: hard - **Rule**: exactly one implementation parses any given state file, and it lives in `viewer/parsers.py`. A `bin/` tool that needs a fact imports it. - **Rationale**: two parsers of `BOARD.md` disagreed in production twice, and the disagreement was invisible until a round-trip test one project later. - **Check**: `grep -rn "def parse_" bin/ | grep -v perry_store | grep -v _md_store` - **Known exceptions**: - `release/manage.py` reads `phase/CURRENT` at two git refs with its own "no phase" set: the pointer reader in `viewer/parsers.py` serves a working tree, and `release/` does not import `viewer/` (USER-981, 2026-09-21). - **Sunset (proposed, DESIGN-023)**: becomes false at DESIGN-023 § 6 row H, when `bin/`, the state readers in `viewer/parsers.py` and the state files they read are deleted, and structured state lives only in the kernel's store, read and written through the kernel CLI. Until row H it holds for everything `bin/` still reads. Its successor is `kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 3: nothing but the kernel opens the store, and only `export`, to decide `unchanged`, and `import` read the export. ### NN-2 — The store is truth; the projection is rendered - **Severity**: hard - **Rule**: a mutating command writes the record first. Every reading of it — a payload and `perry-tasks board` — is derived from the record. No command reads, renders or creates a board file; a `BOARD.md` a project still holds is retired, is read only by the import verbs that upgrade the project, and every tool that sees one says it can be deleted. A projection edited by hand is not absorbed: the store is what every reading reports. - **Rationale**: `ADR-007`. Absorbing a hand edit destroys the canonical value; overwriting it destroys the human's intent. Both must be visible. - **Sunset (proposed, DESIGN-023)**: becomes false at DESIGN-023 § 6 row H, when `perry-tasks board`, the `BOARD.md` import verbs and every projection are deleted with `bin/`. The store stays the truth, and nothing is projected from it: readings come from kernel `query`, and the only file derived from the store is the export, which only `export`, to decide `unchanged`, and `import` read (`kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 5.8). ### NN-3 — A write that cannot do what it claims refuses - **Severity**: hard - **Rule**: no command reports a write it did not perform. A render that cannot place every stored record exits non-zero and names what it could not place. - **Rationale**: `DESIGN-016 § 1.5`. The documented recovery command reported `rendered … from 399 stored record(s)`, exit 0, having restored none of 151 deleted rows. ### NN-4 — Deterministic tools decide nothing about meaning - **Severity**: hard - **Rule**: `bin/` makes only mechanical judgements. Whether a summary reads like prose, whether a spec's scope is adequate, whether an ADR applies — all belong to an agent or the user. - **Rationale**: `DESIGN-014`. Five rounds of regex lost to a full stop. - **Known exceptions**: `perry-codex-preflight` shells out to `codex exec` to check the CLI is alive. It judges nothing; it pings. ### NN-5 — The suite never writes into the tree it runs in - **Severity**: hard - **Rule**: every test writes to a temporary root. `tests/tree_guard.py` runs on every exit path and fails the suite otherwise. - **Rationale**: an un-rooted `perry-task` call once discharged real board rows on every run for months, invisibly, because the sweep is idempotent. ### NN-6 — An agent may describe this file, and may not decide it - **Severity**: hard - **Rule**: an agent writes and rewrites the descriptive sections (§2, §4, §5's shapes, §8) freely. It may ADD to §6 and §7, marked `proposed`, and may delete from neither. Changing §1, a `Forbidden` line in §3, a contract version in §5, or a confirmed rule in §6 is a question for the user, asked before the change lands. - **Rationale**: the agent doing the typing is what makes this document affordable, and the agent being unable to overrule it is what keeps it from becoming a mirror. A description follows the code and can refuse nothing; this file has to be able to refuse. DESIGN-017 carries the argument. ## §7. Open questions - **OQ-1 — The schema anchors this file in the wrong place.** *Closed 2026-09-21 (USER-987).* TASK-451 (DESIGN-017 A1, main 6d471770) anchors `ARCHITECTURE.md` at the code root in `schema/state-schema.json`; TASK-452 (A2, main 5d661ec6) makes `perry-state` read and cap-check it there, and `--section architecture` reports `exists: true` on this repository. `perry-diagnose`'s ownership scan, the last reader that ignored the code anchor, was fixed by TASK-477 (main a2a12a8f). The text below is the question as it stood. ANSWERED for where it lives, open for the fix. `schema/state-schema.json § files[id=architecture]` and `§ claims` both anchor `ARCHITECTURE.md` at the STATE root; `packs/software-ops/architecture.md` says "at the project root". The user settled the question on 2026-09-09: an architecture document describes code, so it lives at the code root, and `perry/` holds runtime state only. That makes the schema's `anchor: state` the defect — and while it stands, `perry-state --section architecture` reports `exists: false` on a project that has one. Note `.perry/config.jsonl` already separates `pmo_repo_path` from `code_repo_path`, so the resolution rule has somewhere to read from. No row is open for this yet. - **OQ-2 — What is the module document's contract?** This file links `bin/ARCHITECTURE.md`, and nothing yet declares its shape, its cap, its owner, or what happens when it drifts from the code beside it. *Partly answered 2026-09-21 (USER-978):* a component §2 declares no module document for has none — an architecture reviewer does not count its absence as missing context. Shape, cap, owner and drift stay open. - **OQ-3 — Should `perry-lint` check mermaid?** `perry-state` already counts fenced mermaid blocks (`mermaid_count`) and nothing consumes the number. - **OQ-4 — May `--compact` be accepted with `--section next`?** *Proposed* (TASK-442). `DESIGN-020 § 5.4`'s closing step runs `perry-state --section next --after --compact`, and `perry-state` refuses `--compact` together with `--section`. `TASK-443` builds that step and needs one of the two to give way. - **OQ-5 — Should the contract registry recognise a family that is not `/list`?** *Proposed* (TASK-442). `perry-next/1.0` is one object, not a list. `tests/contract_key_parity.py § CONTRACT_ID` matches only a three-part id, so the parity baseline keys `schema/next-contract.md` by its path, and two registry tests had their `/list` assumption widened to take the page at all. - **OQ-6 — May `--section ` print something other than the payload's key?** *Proposed* (TASK-442). §4 describes a section as one key in full. `--section next` with `--lane` or `--after` prints a block evaluated over fewer rules, which is not what `--json` carries under `next`. - **OQ-7 — Does the phase heartbeat survive the move to `--section next`?** *Proposed* (TASK-442). `goals/SKILL.md` prompted a phase snapshot after `phase_heartbeat_days`. That prompt is now the rule `R-phase-heartbeat`, but no value in `perry-state`'s payload dates the last snapshot, so the rule reports its fact unknown and never fires. Keeping it needs `perry-state` to compute that date; dropping it means deleting the rule. - **OQ-8 — What covers the lane lines that name a command with no rule behind them?** *Proposed* (TASK-442). Two kinds are marked and waiting. **After a subcommand**: `goals/SKILL.md`'s `score-phase` row and `goals/reference/phases.md` step 9, both naming `plan-phase`. They are the proactive closing step `TASK-443` builds; when it ships it renders `--after score-phase` and the two lines go. **In a standup's next-step position**: an ADR whose sunset date has passed and the old-style `DECISIONS.md` migration, both in `decide/reference/decisions.md`, and the undigested `inputs/` and stale-digest counts in `work/reference/digests.md`. `reference/next-rules.json` has a rule for none of the four, and **the reason is the bound, not a missing fact**: `DESIGN-020 § 5.3`'s table is what `TASK-442` was bounded to and names none of them, so each is a later row's work. Two of the four already have their fact — `decisions.expired_sunsets` for the sunset, and `operations.inputs` with `operations.inputs_oldest` and `operations.inputs_oldest_days` for the digests. Stale digests have no count in the payload, only per-card staleness under `roles.cards[].knowledge[]`, and the migration has no fact at all; those two need a fact as well as a rule. *Proposed — partly answered 2026-09-23 (TASK-484):* one of the four now has its rule — the undigested `inputs/` line, through `R-inputs-waiting` over the facts `operations.inputs` and `operations.first_input`, and `work/reference/digests.md` was rewritten to stop saying the opposite. The expired-sunset ADR, the `DECISIONS.md` migration and the stale-digest count stay open, and the sentence above holds for those three. ## §8. # Architecture — Perry

> DESIGN-023 H source candidate. Descriptive reconciliation is authorized by
> TASK-494; changed targets remain visible for independent review and the user's
> final H/V5 decision. This file does not record acceptance or live activation.
> Prior confirmed text is immutable at base b9be4d39f52ce1266534215b999c9db408b03bc5.

## §1. Mission & scope

Perry is a virtual project office for solo and small projects. The skill supplies
method and judgment; the generic kernel stores structured state. Markdown holds
narrative, evidence and user decisions. The kernel uses Python's standard library,
SQLite and a deterministic JSONL export. It runs without markdown or an agent.

The skill supports Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex CLI. Host helpers are optional
skill tools, with no new kernel capability. No server, model API or dependency is
introduced by the split. Project stores remain local to each project anchor.

## §2. Components

| Component | Responsibility | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `bin/perry` | Single thin native entry point | imports `perry_kernel.main`; no dispatch aliases |
| `kernel/` | Generic items, types, fields, transitions, guards, relations, events and attachments | [kernel target](kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md); native `describe` |
| `SKILL.md`, `goals/`, `work/`, `decide/` | Routing, method, meaning, ownership and evidence decisions | lane procedures, [operating rules](reference/operating-rules.md) |
| `templates/process/` | Method as data | template format in native `describe` |
| `tools/` | Host helpers, document safety facts and architecture evidence | [tool contracts](tools/README.md), [helper shapes](tools/helper-contracts.md) |
| `release/` | Perry product versions, updates and publishing | [release rules](release/README.md) |
| `tests/`, `kernel/tests/` | Native/helper correctness and isolated integration | [suite definition](tests/README.md) |
| `perry/`, `.perry/` | Historical project documents and local configuration/evidence | preserved, not rewritten by this candidate |

`viewer/README.md` is a retirement marker, not a browser or parser. The old
`schema/` and typed-state tools are removed in this candidate. Exact finite
proposals and consumer blockers are [the H ledger](release/retirement/README.md).

## §3. Boundaries & dependencies

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  User[User] --> Skill[Skill and process template]
  Skill --> CLI[bin/perry]
  CLI --> Kernel[Generic kernel]
  Kernel --> Store[(Project store)]
  Kernel --> Export[Deterministic export]
  Skill --> Tools[Host and document helpers]
  Tools --> Docs[Documents and source facts]
  Outside[External consumers] --> CLI
```

Allowed: skill and external consumers → native CLI → kernel → store. Helpers
that need structured state call the native CLI with explicit roots. They do not
open SQLite or fold native exports. Architecture tools analyze source as data,
never execute analyzed code. Release tooling is separate product infrastructure.

Forbidden:

- The kernel imports no skill/helper/release module, reads no markdown and runs
  no command. Its eight concepts and existing command/guard budgets do not grow.
- A helper must not become a hidden compatibility command in `bin/`, retain a
  legacy state writer, or copy the old full viewer parser into the skill.
- A figure about current structured state must come from native query/metric
  output. The skill chooses recommendations and records uncertainty explicitly.
- No caller invents actor identity, human acceptance or independent review.
- Roots and stores are explicit in tests. `PERRY_KERNEL_TESTING=1` prevents an
  omitted test store from using the shared live store.

The old single-viewer-parser and JSONL projection rules are replaced by the
kernel's store/export boundary. This is a visible target change under DESIGN-023,
not an author-certified compliance result. Historical documents are retained.

## §4. Data flow

Each project anchor resolves one store shared by its worktrees. The skill applies
the process template and uses item/relation/attachment operations. Native queries
return counts, blockers and metrics. Documents are attached as evidence, never
folded into current item state. Exports are backups and review surfaces; they are
not replication. Import is into an empty store only.

Before reading current project state, run the skill's recovery and interrupted-run
procedure. A legacy transaction marker blocks migration; use a pinned pre-cutover
release to recover it. Never delete it or silently resume a dossier.

## §5. Contracts

`bin/perry describe` is the native versioned argument/result contract. Every
native result is an envelope. Unknown arguments/keys refuse; help does not execute.
A refusal never authorizes direct edits to the store, an export or a legacy file.

Host helper contracts are versioned separately in `tools/helper-contracts.md`.
They are not the retired `schema/*-contract.md` payloads. aiMark must adapt to
these shapes before any live cutover. Kernel source remains unchanged in H.

## §6. Non-negotiables

1. Structured state is owned solely by the kernel. No helper opens its database.
2. Deterministic tools judge shape and facts; evidence adequacy and document meaning
   remain with the skill, an independent reviewer and the actual user.
3. A command never reports a write it did not perform. Structural success is not
   acceptance. No-op and refusal remain distinguishable.
4. Tests use temporary roots/stores and check source-tree integrity on every suite
   exit. Integration tests run a disposable merge of immutable local refs.
5. Lane ownership, high-stakes screening, recovery/interrupted gates, evidence,
   reviewer freshness and named human sign-off are retained. Safety gates cannot
   be dropped. Document helper output does not authenticate consent.
6. Agents may describe architecture; changing a confirmed mission, Forbidden rule,
   contract version or hard target requires the user's actual decision before it
   lands. Candidate text and fresh static receipts do not supply that decision.
7. Do not self-merge. A coding-branch green is not independent combined-tree green.

## §7. Open acceptance boundaries

The concrete drop table, viewer retirement, preference/config procedure and target
reconciliation remain H proposals. Root/F deliveries, aiMark adapters and both
project migration rehearsals must be tested together by an independent integrator.
Live activation, backup/export receipts, rollback limits and the user's V5 are
outside this source executor's authority. No current state is changed here.

## §8. Evidence

The H ledger names the immutable source base, per-file SHA256, exact path mapping,
check dispositions and real red demonstrations. Architecture start/delivery bundles
are durable outside the executor checkout; their static limits remain visible.
Tests/run's new suite is not a claim that the retired legacy full/slow corpus passed.

Raising a number means editing both the test literal and this section, and DESIGN-023 § 7 makes that a revision of the design, not a new row. ## §3. Boundaries & dependencies ```mermaid flowchart TD Skill["skill — SKILL.md, lanes, templates/process/*.json
markdown and data"] -->|"argv + JSON in"| CLI["kernel executable
thin wrapper"] CLI -->|imports| Pkg["perry_kernel
stdlib only"] Pkg -->|"sqlite3, WAL"| Store[("store
<git-common-dir>/perry/<slug>.db")] Pkg -->|"export writes and compares · import loads"| Export[("<state root>/export/
items.jsonl · events.jsonl")] Pkg -.->|"reads .git and commondir
for the path rule"| Git[(".git metadata")] CLI -->|"JSON out"| Skill ``` Skill-side helpers and tests call the native CLI through subprocesses. They never import kernel internals to read a live store. All test/rehearsal calls name temporary `--store` and explicit `--root` with `PERRY_KERNEL_TESTING=1`. The one-shot legacy work importer retires at H; historical receipts remain. aiMark also calls the native CLI as the external consumer required by DESIGN-023 decision 11; it adapts the native response in its own repository. The kernel imports no consumer code. Allowed directions: skill → kernel → store, where each caller named above stands in the skill's place. There are no others. Forbidden: - **Importing anything outside the stdlib and `perry_kernel`**, `bin/`, `viewer/` and `release/` included. **Reading markdown**, in any mode (the suite runs with no `*.md`). - **Running a command.** The kernel makes no `subprocess`, `os.system`, `os.exec*` or `os.spawn*` call. It finds the git common dir by reading `.git` and `commondir` (§ 5.7). The skill runs a measurement's command and writes the value (decision 8). - **Naming a skill path or a template-declared name.** Goal 1's test greps the kernel source for every type, state and field name in the shipped template as a string literal (`"name"` or `'name'`), case-sensitively. A collision is fixed by renaming on the kernel's side. - **Any other path.** The kernel reads only its store, its `--input` file, the `.git` metadata and the export. It writes only the store and `/export/`. Only `import` loads the export; `export` reads its own files only to tell `unchanged` apart. ## §4. Data flow — what happens to one command ```mermaid flowchart TD Argv["argv"] -->|"-h or --help anywhere"| Help["usage generated from the declaration · exit 0"] Argv --> Parse["parse against the command's declaration"] Parse -->|"undeclared flag or positional, or a flag this command does not honour"| Usage["usage · exit 2"] Parse --> Input["read --input: exactly one JSON object"] Input -->|"an undeclared key at any declared level"| Key["unknown_key · exit 2"] Input --> Resolve["resolve the root, then the store (§ 5.7)"] Resolve --> Txn["open the store and check its format
BEGIN IMMEDIATE for a write, a snapshot for a read"] Txn --> Validate["load the applied template · validate kinds, refs, relations
check expect{} (compare-and-set)"] Validate --> Guards["run every guard that applies (§ 5.4)"] Guards -->|"a refuse-mode guard fails"| Refuse["guard_refused · roll back · exit 1"] Guards --> Mint["mint ids in the transaction · write rows · append one event"] Mint -->|"--dry-run"| Roll["roll back · effect: dry_run"] Mint -->|"nothing differs"| Same["no event · effect: unchanged"] Mint --> Commit["COMMIT · effect: written · events: [seq]"] ``` One command is one transaction. A refusal after `BEGIN` rolls back the whole transaction, including the relations and attachments written by the same `item create`, so an edge made at create cannot half-land (DESIGN-015 § 5.3). An unexpected exception is caught at the top, rolled back and reported as `internal`. No traceback reaches the caller (NN-K6). ## §5. Contracts Split out whole on 2026-09-26 (TASK-488), under the overflow convention in the header, to [`architecture/sections/§5-contracts.md`](architecture/sections/§5-contracts.md). It holds 5.1 the envelope, exit codes and error codes · 5.2 the process template, format 1 · 5.3 field kinds · 5.4 guards · 5.5 metrics and the roll-up · 5.6 commands · 5.7 the store · 5.8 export and import · 5.9 the argument for each new claimed path. Every `§ 5.x` in this document, and every `kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 5.x elsewhere, means that file's subsection. ## §6. Non-negotiables Every rule below is **proposed** (NN-6), and none of them binds until the user confirms it. NN-K3 to NN-K8 restate DESIGN-016's argument-contract lessons as rules of this CLI. ### NN-K1 — The kernel knows no method - **Severity**: hard · **Status**: proposed - **Rule**: kernel source names no skill path, and no type, state or field that the shipped template declares (Goal 1). - **Check**: the grep test in § 3, and the kernel suite run with every `*.md` removed. ### NN-K2 — The kernel runs no command and reads no markdown - **Severity**: hard · **Status**: proposed - **Rule**: no process is spawned, whether for a metric or for the git path rule. A `bin/` render once ran when it was asked for help. ### NN-K4 — Nothing undeclared is accepted - **Severity**: hard · **Status**: proposed - **Rule**: every command, read-only ones included, refuses with exit 2 an undeclared flag or positional, a flag it does not honour (`--dry-run` on a read, `--input` on `describe`), and an undeclared input key at any level. An undeclared template key is `template_invalid`, and an undeclared export key is `export_invalid`. Nothing is accepted and then ignored. - **Rationale**: DESIGN-016 § 1.4 and goal 12. `--wrte` printed a render, wrote nothing, and exited 0. ### NN-K5 — An explicit flag beats the environment - **Severity**: hard · **Status**: proposed - **Rule**: `--root` beats `PERRY_PROJECT`, which beats the walk up. `--store` beats `PERRY_STORE`, which beats the derived path (§ 5.7). - **Rationale**: DESIGN-016 goal 1. Two checkouts once minted the same id (DESIGN-023 § 1), and Goal 5's concurrent-worktree test holds this rule. ## §7. Open questions - **OQ-K1 — Which metric values fold together? Resolved: the user chose (a) on 2026-09-24, and § 5.5 now defines `rollup`.** DESIGN-022 fixes the fold (§ 5.5). The rule stays fixed; the relation it follows is data. - (c) **Several metrics on one item**, as a `list` of `metric`. This contradicts § 5.4, and list elements have no ids to update one at a time. - (d) **No fold in the kernel.** The skill folds `query` output, against decision 8 ("fixes how several … roll up") and root § 3 (a lane does not compute a number). Two further questions follow from the answer and stay open: a second-level count, like DESIGN-022 § 5.2's per-grouping counts that exclude items by a field, and whether `count_by` may count by `rollup.met`. - **OQ-K2 — The age of a measurement.** DESIGN-022's `due` state needs the time at which `current` last changed. Either (a) the skill reads it from `events` (`keys: ["field:"]`) and applies its own threshold, which works today, or (b) the metric output gains a derived `current_at`, a key decision 8 does not name. - **OQ-K3 — Where the count of unexported events lives.** DESIGN-023 § 5.3 has `describe` report it, and § 5.1 makes `describe` byte-identical across projects; both cannot hold. Resolved: the user answered on 2026-09-24 — an event of the run's own session fails the suite, another session's is reported — and `kernel/tests/livestore.py` implements it.** The store is shared. If another worktree wrote during a test run, detection saw a leak and the run went red. Prevention is exact. The question was whether detection should report the new events or fail the suite. - **OQ-K5 — Readings where DESIGN-023 is silent.** Each can be reversed. `limit.per` is a list, so decision 9's "a named field" can mean more than one. # Architecture — `kernel/` § 5. Contracts

> Section file of [`kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../ARCHITECTURE.md), split from it whole on 2026-09-26 (TASK-488).
> Overflow convention: the root document's — split per § to `architecture/sections/§<N>-<topic>.md` — mirrored under `kernel/`.
> Cap: ≤ 600 lines, the module-document cap. A citation of `kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 5.x resolves here.

## §5. Contracts

### 5.1 The envelope, exit codes and error codes

Every command writes exactly one JSON object to stdout, with or without `--json`, and that
object is the whole answer. Anything a program must act on, warnings included, is a field
in it. On a refusal, stderr also carries one line, `kernel: <code>: <message>`, which
repeats `error` for a human. Every key is always present.

```json
{"ok": true, "surface": "1.0", "command": "item move", "effect": "written",
 "events": [57], "store_seq": 57, "warnings": [], "result": {"item": {"…": "…"}},
 "error": null}
```

`effect` is `written` (at least one event committed, or export files replaced),
`unchanged` (a write that found nothing to change and wrote no event), `dry_run` (the
transaction ran and was rolled back), `read`, or `refused`. `events` lists the seq of each
event this command committed, and is empty unless `effect` is `written`. `store_seq` is the
highest event seq visible to the command, after its commit. Reads carry it too, so a poller
can tell a stale read from a fresh one. On a refusal, `ok` is `false`, `result` is `null`,
and `error` is `{"code", "message", "details"}`. Exit codes: `0` success · `1` refused ·
`2` bad invocation · `3` internal fault (rolled back).

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | 2 | an unknown command, an undeclared flag or positional, a flag this command does not honour (`--dry-run` on a read), or a missing flag argument. Also a flag given twice, a flag given an empty value, `--input @` naming no file, an argument that is not valid UTF-8, `PERRY_STORE` or `PERRY_PROJECT` not valid UTF-8, and `PERRY_STORE` set but empty (§ 5.7) |
| `input_invalid` | 2 | `--input` is not exactly one JSON object, or a declared key has the wrong JSON type or a required one is missing. Not one JSON object includes a key given twice, bytes (stdin, an `@file`) that are not UTF-8, a lone surrogate in any string or key, a non-finite number, an integer outside −2⁶³ to 2⁶³−1, and nesting past 64 levels. A command's own input rule is this code too: a `state_root` that is empty, holds a backslash, a line break or a NUL, or is not a relative path inside the anchor, a relation naming both or neither of `to` and `from`, a field in both `set` and `unset`, a negative `limit` or `after_seq`, an `after` that is not an id, and a `where` or `count_by` field given without `type` or naming a `list` or `metric` field |
| `unknown_key` | 2 | the input carries a key the command does not declare, at any declared level. The legal set is named |
| `actor_invalid` | 2 | a write has no `actor`, the actor's `kind` is not `human` or `agent`, its `name` is empty, or an `agent` has no `session` |
| `anchor_not_found` | 1 | no directory holding `.perry/` at `--root`, at `PERRY_PROJECT`, or above the working directory. An empty `PERRY_PROJECT` counts as unset, so the walk runs (§ 5.7) |
| `store_missing` | 1 | the resolved store has not been initialised |
| `store_foreign` | 1 | the file at the store path is not a kernel store. It is never overwritten |
| `store_version` | 1 | the store's format is newer than this kernel |
| `store_busy` | 1 | the write lock was not acquired within 5 s |
| `store_corrupt` | 1 | `sqlite3` reports damage, the kernel's tables are incomplete, `journal_mode=WAL` or `synchronous=FULL` cannot be set, or a row cannot be read back, a recorded `export_token` that is not 16 lowercase hex characters included |
| `store_live_under_test` | 1 | `PERRY_KERNEL_TESTING` is set, empty included, and the store path was derived, not named (§ 5.7) |
| `store_initialized` | 1 | `init` on a store initialised with a different state root |
| `store_not_empty` | 1 | `import` into a store that holds any event |
| `io_error` | 1 | a file the command must read or write could not be. The path is named |
| `no_template` | 1 | an item, relation, attachment or query command before any template is applied |
| `template_invalid` | 1 | the template breaks § 5.2. `details.problems[]` lists each as `{path, message}` |
| `template_version` | 1 | `version` is not above the applied one, or equals it with different content |
| `template_incompatible` | 1 | the new version would strand stored data (§ 5.2). The affected items are named |
| `item_not_found` | 1 | an id in the input, a `ref` value or a relation end does not exist |
| `id_exhausted` | 1 | `item create` would mint an id above 2⁵³, the highest number an id may carry and the highest `import` accepts, so a store never holds an id its own export could not import. `details` names the `type`, `prefix` and `ceiling`; other types go on minting. It is part of the unreleased `surface` 1.0, not a minor bump (the user accepted it on 2026-09-26) |
| `unknown_type` · `unknown_field` · `unknown_transition` · `unknown_relation` | 1 | the applied template does not declare that name |
| `field_invalid` | 1 | a value does not fit its field's kind (§ 5.3) |
| `metric_invalid` | 1 | a metric value breaks § 5.5 |
| `transition_not_allowed` | 1 | the item's state is not in the transition's `from` |
| `guard_refused` | 1 | one or more refuse-mode guards failed. `details.guards[]` lists every one (§ 5.4) |
| `relation_invalid` | 1 | a self-edge, an end whose type the declaration does not allow, or a second `parent` |
| `relation_cycle` | 1 | a `blocks` or `parent` edge would close a cycle |
| `stale_write` | 1 | an item named in `expect` has moved: its `seq` is not the one the caller read |
| `attachment_invalid` | 1 | an empty `ref`, a `ref` containing a line break, or a malformed `hash` |
| `export_dir_foreign` | 1 | `<state root>/export/` holds an entry other than the kernel's two files and a temporary file named with the store's recorded token |
| `export_missing` · `export_invalid` | 1 | `import` finds no export, or a line, a seq run or a replayed change that breaks § 5.8 |
| `replay_mismatch` | 1 | replaying the events does not reproduce `items.jsonl`. The first differing id is named |
| `internal` | 3 | an unexpected fault. The transaction was rolled back |

§ 5.6 cites three error sets. **A** is `usage`, `input_invalid`, `unknown_key` and
`internal`. **S** is A plus `anchor_not_found`, `store_missing`, `store_foreign`,
`store_version`, `store_busy`, `store_corrupt`, `store_live_under_test` and `io_error`.
**W** is S plus `actor_invalid`. The only warning code is
`limit_exceeded`.

### 5.2 The process template — format 1

```json
{"format": 1, "name": "workshop", "version": 3,
 "types": {
  "widget": {
   "prefix": "W", "digits": 3,
   "states": ["queued", "cutting", "polished", "shipped", "scrapped"],
   "initial": "queued", "terminal": ["shipped", "scrapped"],
   "fields": {
    "size":      {"kind": "enum", "values": ["XS", "S", "M", "L"], "ordered": true},
    "bench":     {"kind": "enum", "values": ["north", "south"]},
    "fragile":   {"kind": "enum", "values": [false, true]},
    "inspector": {"kind": "actor"},
    "ship_by":   {"kind": "date"},
    "made_from": {"kind": "ref", "to": ["widget"]},
    "colors":    {"kind": "list", "of": {"kind": "text"}},
    "weight_g":  {"kind": "number"}},
   "create_guards": [{"kind": "required", "fields": ["bench"]}],
   "transitions": {
    "start":  {"from": ["queued"], "to": "cutting", "guards": [
      {"kind": "relations_closed", "relation": "blocks", "direction": "incoming"},
      {"kind": "limit", "max": 2, "per": ["bench"], "mode": "warn"}]},
    "polish": {"from": ["cutting"], "to": "polished", "guards": []},
    "ship":   {"from": ["polished"], "to": "shipped", "guards": [
      {"kind": "required", "fields": ["inspector"], "at_least": {"size": "S"}},
      {"kind": "actor", "actor_kind": "human", "when": {"fragile": [true]}},
      {"kind": "relations_closed", "relation": "parent", "direction": "incoming"}]},
    "scrap":  {"from": ["queued", "cutting", "polished"], "to": "scrapped", "guards": []}}},
  "gauge": {
   "prefix": "G", "states": ["live", "retired"], "initial": "live", "terminal": ["retired"],
   "fields": {"reading": {"kind": "metric"}},
   "transitions": {"retire": {"from": ["live"], "to": "retired", "guards": []}}}},
 "relations": {"pairs_with": {"from": ["widget"], "to": ["widget"]}}}
```

| Rule | |
|---|---|
| Keys | Only the keys shown are legal, at every level. `digits` (default 1) and `create_guards` (default `[]`) may be left out. An unknown key is `template_invalid` |
| Names | Types, fields, states, transitions and relation kinds match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$`. `id`, `type` and `state` cannot be field names. `blocks` and `parent` cannot be declared |
| Prefixes | match `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{0,9}$` and are unique across types. An id is `<prefix>-<n>`, where `n` is zero-padded to `digits` and grows past it (`W-999`, `W-1000`) |
| States | `initial` ∈ `states`. `terminal` is a non-empty subset of `states`. Every transition's `from` ⊆ `states`, and its `to` ∈ `states` |
| Relations | A declared kind lists the types allowed at its `from` and `to` ends. `blocks` and `parent` connect items of any types |
| Guards | § 5.4. Every field a guard names must be declared on the guard's type |
| Apply | `version` must rise. Re-applying the identical template is `unchanged`. Guards govern writes, not stored state, so existing items are not re-checked |
| Compatibility | A new version is `template_incompatible` while stored data depends on what it drops. It cannot remove a type that has items, a state that items occupy, a field that holds a value, an enum value in use, a `ref` target type in use, or a relation kind that has edges. It cannot change the kind of a field that holds a value, or the `prefix` or `digits` of a type that has items. Adding is always compatible (Goal 4) |

### 5.3 Field kinds and their values

| Kind | Options | Value | Set when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | — | a JSON string | non-empty after trimming whitespace |
| `int` | — | a JSON integer (not a boolean), with \|n\| ≤ 2⁵³ | not `null` |
| `number` | — | a finite JSON number | not `null` |
| `date` | — | a valid calendar date, `YYYY-MM-DD` | not `null` |
| `enum` | `values` (strings or booleans, unique), `ordered` (default `false`) | one of `values` | not `null` |
| `actor` | — | `{"kind": "human" \| "agent", "name", "session"}`, with `session` required for `agent` | not `null` |
| `ref` | `to` (type names) | the id of an existing item of one of those types | not `null` |
| `list` | `of`: one element declaration of any kind except `list` and `metric` | a JSON array of such values | non-empty |
| `metric` | — | `{"current", "target", "baseline", "direction"}` (§ 5.5) | `current` is not `null` |

There is no boolean kind. A flag is an `enum` with `values: [false, true]`, as in
`when: {"fragile": [true]}` (decision 9). `set` replaces a field's value whole, except for a
`metric`: the keys given are merged into the stored value, so a measurement can write
`{"current": 8}` alone. The first `set` of a metric must carry `target` and `direction`.

### 5.4 Guards

| Kind | Keys | Refuses unless |
|---|---|---|
| `required` | `fields[]`, `at_least{}` (at least one is non-empty) | every listed field is set (§ 5.3), and every `at_least` field is an ordered enum whose value is set and sits at or after the named minimum in `values` |
| `actor` | `actor_kind` and/or `name` | the command's actor has that `kind` and/or exactly that `name`. The actor is caller-declared, so this names a person but does not authenticate one (DESIGN-023 § 5.2) |
| `relations_closed` | `relation`, `direction` (`incoming` or `outgoing`) | every item at the other end of an edge of that kind is in a terminal state. `incoming` means edges whose `to` is this item, such as a `blocks` edge's blockers or a `parent` edge's children. `outgoing` means edges whose `from` is this item |
| `limit` | `max` (an integer ≥ 1), `per[]` (field names, possibly none), `mode` (`refuse` or `warn`) | counting this item, no more than `max` items of its type would sit in the target state with the same values of the `per` fields. `warn` proceeds and reports `limit_exceeded` |

- **`when`.** Any guard may carry one `when`: exactly one field of the item, mapped to a
  list of values, where `null` matches unset. The guard applies only when the item's value
  is in that list. Neither `when` nor `per` may name a `list` or a `metric` field.
- **When and on what.** A type's `create_guards` run on `item create`, with `initial` as
  the target state, and a transition's `guards` run on `item move`. Guards see the item as
  the command would leave it, including fields and relations set by the same command.
- **Reporting.** Every guard is evaluated. When any refuse-mode guard fails,
  `details.guards[]` lists each failure as `{"index", "kind", "when", "detail"}`:
  - `required`: `{"missing": [...], "below": {"size": {"value": "XS", "at_least": "S"}}}`;
  - `actor`: `{"actor": {...}, "needs": {...}}`; `relations_closed`: `{"not_terminal": ["W-3"]}`;
  - `limit`: `{"count": 3, "max": 2, "values": {"bench": "north"}}`.

  When a warn-mode `limit` fails and nothing refuses, the command succeeds and the failure
  lands in `warnings[]` and on the event.

### 5.5 Metrics: the formula and the roll-up

This section is derived from DESIGN-022 § 5.1 and § 5.2. The rule is fixed, and no template
key changes it.

A metric value is `{"current": number|null, "target": number, "baseline": number|null,
"direction": "up"|"down"}`. It is `metric_invalid` when `target` or `direction` is
missing, a key is unknown, a number is not finite, or `baseline` is set and `target` is not
beyond it in `direction` (above it for `up`, below it for `down`).

DESIGN-022's five directions map onto these two without loss, because the baseline is what
tells a trend from a limit:

| DESIGN-022 | Here |
|---|---|
| `increase` · `decrease` | `up` · `down`, with a `baseline` |
| `at_least` · `at_most` | `up` · `down`, with `baseline: null` |
| the milestone direction | `up`, `target: 1`, `baseline: null`, `current` 0 or 1 |

```
met       null when current is null · up: current >= target · down: current <= target
fraction  null when current or baseline is null; otherwise
          raw = (current - baseline) / (target - baseline)
          0.0 if raw <= 0 · 1.0 if raw >= 1 · else round(raw, 3) clamped to [0.001, 0.999]
          (0.0 and 1.0 are reserved for the exact ends, as DESIGN-022 publishes them)
```

`item get` and `query` return `met` and `fraction` inside the metric's value. Neither is
stored or exported. The kernel never runs a command. The skill runs a measurement's
declared command, then writes `current` with `item update` and passes the command in
`note`. The event records it, so DESIGN-022's rule that only a command measures still holds.

**The roll-up.** DESIGN-022 User Decision 2 folds several measured conditions into one
answer. An item's `rollup` folds the metric fields of the items whose `parent` it is, one
level down, whatever their state (OQ-K1, option (a), answered by the user on 2026-09-24).
Every metric field declared on a child's type is one member, and an unset one is
unmeasured; the item's own metric fields are not members, and no template key changes any
of this. `rollup` is `null` when no child's type declares a metric field, and otherwise
`{"members", "measured", "met", "fraction"}`. `measured` counts members with a `current`.
`met` is `null` when any member is unmeasured, `true` when every member is met, and `false`
otherwise. `fraction` is the single member's `fraction` when there is exactly one member,
and `null` otherwise. It is never a mean.

### 5.6 Commands

**Flags.** `--store PATH` and `--root PATH` (§ 5.7), `--json`, and `-h` / `--help` apply to
every command. `--input JSON|@FILE|-` (inline JSON, a file, or stdin) is taken only where a
command has input, and `--dry-run` only on writes.

**Common write keys.** A write that appends its own event (every write but `export` and
`import`) takes `actor` (required, § 5.3) and `note` (optional text, stored on the event).
The item, `rel` and `attach` writes also take `expect` (optional, `{"<id>": <seq>}`), which
is compare-and-set: each named item's `seq` must still be the one the caller read, or the
write is refused as `stale_write`.

**Items in `result`.** An item carries the § 2 keys plus `relations[]` (every edge touching
it, as `{kind, from, to}`), `attachments[]`, `startable`, `blocked_by` and `rollup`.
`blocked_by` lists, sorted, the non-terminal items that have a `blocks` edge to this item.
`startable` is true when the item is in its type's `initial` state and `blocked_by` is
empty.

| Command | Input | `result` | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|
| `init` | `actor`, `state_root` (a relative path inside the anchor) | `store`, `anchor`, `state_root`, `journal_mode` | A, `anchor_not_found`, `store_foreign`, `store_version`, `store_busy`, `store_corrupt`, `store_live_under_test`, `io_error`, `actor_invalid`, `store_initialized` |
| `template apply` | `actor`, `template`, `note` | `name`, `version`, `previous_version` | W, `template_invalid`, `template_version`, `template_incompatible` |
| `template show` | — | `template` (the applied one, verbatim), `version`, `applied_seq`, `applied_at`. All four are `null` before the first apply | S |
| `template validate` | `template` | `valid: true`, `format`, `types` (a count). It checks the format only and opens no store. `template apply --dry-run` tests compatibility | A, `io_error`, `template_invalid` |
| `item create` | `actor`, `type`, `fields{}`, `relations[]` (`{kind, to}` or `{kind, from}`, where the new item is the other end), `attachments[]` (`{ref, hash?}`), `note`, `expect` | `item` | W, `stale_write`, `no_template`, `unknown_type`, `unknown_field`, `field_invalid`, `metric_invalid`, `item_not_found`, `unknown_relation`, `relation_invalid`, `relation_cycle`, `attachment_invalid`, `guard_refused`, `id_exhausted` |
| `item get` | `id` | `item` | S, `no_template`, `item_not_found` |
| `item update` | `actor`, `id`, `set{}`, `unset[]`, `note`, `expect`. No guards run | `item` | W, `stale_write`, `no_template`, `item_not_found`, `unknown_field`, `field_invalid`, `metric_invalid` |
| `item move` | `actor`, `id`, `transition`, `set{}`, `unset[]`, `note`, `expect` | `item`, `transition`, `from_state`, `to_state` | W, `stale_write`, `no_template`, `item_not_found`, `unknown_transition`, `transition_not_allowed`, `unknown_field`, `field_invalid`, `metric_invalid`, `guard_refused` |
| `rel add` · `rel remove` | `actor`, `kind`, `from`, `to`, `note`, `expect`. Adding an existing edge, or removing a missing one, is `unchanged` | `relation` | W, `stale_write`, `no_template`, `item_not_found`, `unknown_relation`, `relation_invalid`, `relation_cycle` (on add) |
| `attach add` · `attach remove` | `actor`, `id`, `ref`, `hash` (on add), `note`, `expect` | `attachment` | W, `stale_write`, `no_template`, `item_not_found`, `attachment_invalid` |
| `query` | `type`, `ids[]`, `state[]`, `terminal`, `where{field: [values]}`, `related` (`{kind, to}` or `{kind, from}`), `startable`, `count_by[]`, `after`, `limit` | `items[]`, `total`, `returned`, `truncated`, `next_after`, `counts[]` | S, `no_template`, `unknown_type`, `unknown_field`, `unknown_relation`, `item_not_found` |
| `events` | `items[]`, `keys[]` (key prefixes), `commands[]`, `after_seq`, `limit` | `events[]`, `total`, `returned`, `truncated`, `next_after_seq`, `last_export_seq`, `unexported` | S |
| `export` | — | `dir`, `files{name: {lines, bytes, sha256}}`, `last_export_seq`. It is `unchanged` when both files already hold these bytes | S, `export_dir_foreign` |
| `import` | `state_root` | `dir`, `items`, `events`, `last_seq`, `verified: true` | A, `anchor_not_found`, `store_foreign`, `store_version`, `store_busy`, `store_corrupt`, `store_live_under_test`, `io_error`, `store_not_empty`, `export_missing`, `export_invalid`, `replay_mismatch` |
| `describe` | — (no `--input`, and no store is opened) | `surface`, `concepts`, `budget`, `commands[]`, `flags`, `env`, `exit_codes`, `errors`, `template_format` | A |

**Reads.** In `query`, separate filters are ANDed and the values within one filter are
ORed. There is no expression language. A `where` or `count_by` that names a field needs
`type`. `counts[]` is `[{"key": {...}, "n": N}]`, counted over every match before the
bound, and `count_by` takes `type`, `state` or any field that is not a `list` or `metric`.
Items are ordered by prefix, then number, and `after` continues from an id. `query` and
`events` return at most 50 rows unless `limit` says otherwise (`limit: 0` asks for
everything), and `total` and `truncated` are always present.

**`describe`** reports the command surface only, so it is byte-identical in every project:
it never reads a store, a path or a clock.
- Each entry of `commands[]` carries `name`, `kind` (`read` or `write`), `purpose`, its flags,
  its input keys with JSON types and `required` markers, its `result` keys and its error codes.
- `template_format` carries `format`, `field_kinds`, `guard_kinds`, the built-in relations
  and the template's key schema.
- `surface` is versioned under DESIGN-005's rules (decision 11). Every key is always
  present, and a minor version only adds, which includes adding an optional input.
  **Making an input required, or removing one, is a major change, and a major bump is
  refused without the user.**
- `describe` and `template show` are the only places the skill learns the data model
  (DESIGN-023 § 5.1).

**Events.** A change `key` is `type`, `state`, `field:<name>`, `rel:<kind>:<from>:<to>`
(value `false`/`true`), `attach:<ref>` (value `null`/`{"hash"}`), `template` (`before` is
the previous version and `after` the full template), `state_root` (written by `init`) or
`ceiling:<prefix>`. `items[]` names every item the event touched, and each one's `seq`
becomes the event's seq.

### 5.7 The store

- **The anchor** is `--root`, else `PERRY_PROJECT`, else the first directory at or above
  the working directory that holds `.perry/`; it must hold `.perry/` (`anchor_not_found`).
  ADR-002 still holds: a project is a folder with a `.perry/` anchor, and nothing lists
  projects. **The path** is `--store`, else `PERRY_STORE`, else `<common>/perry/<slug>.db`
  inside git and `<anchor>/.perry/perry.db` outside it.
- **An empty variable** is read per variable, never by truthiness (the user's decision,
  2026-09-25). An empty `PERRY_STORE` is refused with `usage`, as `--store ""` is, so an
  empty value never falls through to the derived, shared store. An empty `PERRY_PROJECT`
  counts as unset, as `bin/lib § resolve_project_root` treats it, and the walk runs. An
  empty `PERRY_KERNEL_TESTING` counts as set: it is a safety switch, and a switch that is
  present fails safe (accepted by the user on 2026-09-26). `--root` is read before
  `PERRY_PROJECT` and `--store` before `PERRY_STORE`, and a variable whose flag is given is
  not read, so it cannot refuse the command.
- **`<common>`** is what `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` prints, read instead of run. The
  kernel walks up from the anchor to `.git` and, if `.git` is a file, follows its `gitdir:`
  line. If that git dir holds `commondir`, the common dir is that path resolved against
  the git dir; otherwise it is the git dir. `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_COMMON_DIR` are ignored. A
  test compares the result with `git rev-parse` on a main worktree, a linked worktree and
  a submodule.
- **`<slug>`** is `root` for a worktree's top level. For any other anchor it is
  `root/<path from the top level>`, with every byte outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` (including
  `/`) written as `%XX`. For example, `tests/fixtures/alpha` becomes
  `root%2Ftests%2Ffixtures%2Falpha`. The slug is injective. Every worktree resolves the
  same file, and each fixture project gets its own (DESIGN-023 § 5.3).
- **Opening.** `init` creates the parent directory and the file and sets
  `journal_mode=WAL`. Opening a store checks WAL, `synchronous=FULL` and the format marker
  (`PRAGMA application_id` and `user_version`). A foreign file is refused.
- **Transactions.** A write is one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction with a 5 s busy timeout
  (`store_busy`), so the lock spans the read, the decision and the write. A read is one
  snapshot. Under WAL, a reader in one worktree sees another worktree's commit at once
  (Goal 5). Opening a store probes it and then begins the transaction. The open's
  deadline is set before it probes, so a probe that waited on a busy store leaves the
  open's own retries only the rest of the 5 s, not a whole 5 s more.
- **Ids.** The store keeps a ceiling per prefix. An id is minted inside the write
  transaction as `ceiling + 1`, so two writers cannot mint the same id. A ceiling is never
  lowered, an id is never reused, and no command deletes an item. A `ceiling:<prefix>`
  event raises a ceiling above the stored ids. No command writes one: it arrives only by
  `import`, in an export that DESIGN-023 § 6 row D's importer builds to seed ids that were
  issued and later purged (§ 5.8). `--dry-run` reports the id it would mint unreserved.
- **Tables.** `meta` (format, `state_root`, `last_export_seq`, `export_token`), `template`,
  `item`, `value`, `relation`, `attachment`, `event` and `ceiling`. Row B owns the columns.
  `export_token` is 16 hex characters, recorded at `init` and replaced at `import`; a store
  made before it existed gets one at its first `export` (§ 5.8, § 5.9).
- **The live-store check, which tests rely on,** has two layers:
  - **Prevention.** Kernel tests, and fresh-context reviewers who corrupt a store on
    purpose, always pass `--store <tmp>`. The harness sets `PERRY_KERNEL_TESTING=1`, under
    which a derived path is refused (`store_live_under_test`), so a call that forgets
    `--store` fails instead of writing the shared store. The variable counts as set when it
    is present, empty included. `bin/perry-kernel-migrate`, DESIGN-023 § 6 row D's one-shot
    importer, is not a test, and it sets `PERRY_KERNEL_TESTING=1` on every kernel call as
    the same safety switch. Each of its calls names `--store` under its scratch `--work`
    directory, so a call that lost the flag is refused rather than derived to the live store.
  - **Detection.** The harness reads the live store's highest event seq read-only before
    and after the run. A new event whose actor carries the run's own session fails the
    suite; one from any other session is reported, not failed (OQ-K4). This is the
    kernel's `tests/tree_guard.py`, which cannot see inside `.git/` (DESIGN-023 § 5.3).

### 5.8 Export and import

- **`export`** writes exactly two files, `<anchor>/<state_root>/export/items.jsonl` and
  `events.jsonl`, and then records `last_export_seq`. Each is written to a temporary name
  carrying a token the store recorded at `init` or `import`, then renamed into place. It refuses (`export_dir_foreign`) if
  the directory holds any other entry, except such a temporary file, left by a crashed export, which it removes.
- **The bytes are deterministic.** Each line is one JSON object with sorted keys, `,` and
  `:` separators, UTF-8 without ASCII escaping and a `\n` ending, and numbers are written
  as stored. `items.jsonl` is sorted by prefix, then number, one
  `{id, type, state, fields, relations, attachments, created_at, updated_at, seq}` per line,
  with only outgoing edges (`{kind, to}`) and no derived key. `events.jsonl` is sorted by
  `seq`. Two exports of an unchanged store are byte-identical.
- **`import`** needs an empty store: the file is absent or holds no event
  (`store_not_empty`). In one transaction it:
  1. reads `<anchor>/<state_root>/export/`, and checks that the seqs run 1…n without a gap
     and that event 1 is the `init` for this `state_root` (`export_invalid`);
  2. replays every change by seq, checking that each `before` equals the replayed value,
     without re-running guards, because the history was written under earlier templates.
     Each change is held instead to the template in force when its event was written,
     the last one the replay has applied, as a live write of it would have been:
     - a `template` whose version rises above the one in force and strands no stored
       data (§ 5.2). The first `template` change has no version in force to rise above,
       and is held only to being a valid template;
     - a `type` set once, on an item that does not exist yet, that the template declares,
       on an id that type mints (its prefix, padded to its `digits`);
     - a `state` of the item's type, and a `field:` its type declares, with a value that
       fits the field's kind (§ 5.3) in the form a live write stores; a `null` value is
       held only to the field being declared;
     - on an edge being added, a relation kind the template knows, with ends a declared
       kind allows. Removing an edge is held only to the no-op rule below;
     - an `attach:` ref that `attach add` and `attach remove` would take: not empty or
       only white space, and holding no line break.

     An event that holds a `template` change and any item change (`type`, `state`,
     `field:`, `rel:` or `attach:`) is refused as a line that breaks this section, before
     any replay: `template apply` writes its change alone, and no other command writes a
     `template` change (TASK-489 round 6). So the template in force is the same for every
     item change of an event. The item's type is the stored one, or, for the event's own
     item (`items[0]`), the `type` the same event sets, so a change replayed before its
     item's `type` change is checked as it would be after it (TASK-489 round 5). With
     both rules, where an item change sits inside its event does not decide whether it is
     checked, or against which template. A change to an item that has
     no type and gets none in its event is refused by the store, which leaves no item
     without a type and a state. A `state_root` change and a `ceiling:` value are held
     only to their shape (step 1's line checks). A relation change that flips nothing
     (`before` equal to `after`) is refused for every kind, because no command writes one
     (NN-K8). Each refusal is `export_invalid` and names the event's `seq` and the
     change's `key`, except the mixed-event refusal, which names the line, as step 1's
     line checks do (TASK-489);
  3. sets each ceiling to the higher of the largest id replayed and the largest
     `ceiling:<prefix>` value;
  4. serialises the replayed items as `export` would and compares them byte for byte with
     `items.jsonl` (`replay_mismatch`).

  `import` writes no event of its own, so export, import and a second export are
  byte-identical (Goal 3).
- **Only `import` loads the export;** `export` reads it only to decide `unchanged`. Committing it is the user's choice (DESIGN-023
  § 5.3). `events` reports `unexported`, the events written since the last export (OQ-K3).

### 5.9 The argument for each new claimed path (ADR-016)

**`<git-common-dir>/perry/<slug>.db`**
- **Why this path, and not a claim Perry already holds.** The existing claims, the state
  root and `.perry/`, sit in the worktree and follow the branch, so a store there gives
  every checkout its own copy and lock. That is how two checkouts minted the same id while
  `git merge` saw two lines of text, not one contested identity (DESIGN-023 § 1, item 3).
  The git common dir is the one place every worktree of a repository resolves to, and git
  keeps nothing under `perry/` there. Outside git, `<anchor>/.perry/perry.db` is a new
  file inside the existing `.perry/` claim, not a new claimed path.
- **The cost to a project that has a file of that name.** A foreign file is refused
  (`store_foreign`) and never overwritten. The directory is invisible to `git status` and
  lost on a fresh clone, which is why the export exists and `events` reports what is
  unexported (DESIGN-023 § 7). **Reversal:** `export`, remove the directory, `import`.

**`<state root>/export/`**
- **Why this path.** The export is the backup and the surface for reading changes, so it
  must sit in the worktree where it can be committed. The state root is already Perry's
  claim (DESIGN-002), so this is a subdirectory of an existing claim, not a new top-level
  name. It is not under `.perry/`, because committing it is the project's choice.
- **The cost to a project that has a file of that name.** A project's own `export/` under
  its state root is kept: `export` refuses (`export_dir_foreign`) while any other entry is there,
  and reads its own two files only to decide `unchanged`. **The one exception is the token.**
  `export` writes each file as `.<file>.<token>.tmp`, where the token is the one the store
  recorded (`meta.export_token`, § 5.7), and it removes only a leftover carrying that token,
  which a crashed export of this store left. It removes nothing else, and an entry with any
  other token is foreign. A store with no recorded token removes nothing on its first
  export, which records one (the user accepted this design on 2026-09-26). **Reversal:**
  delete the directory; only `import` loads it.

Neither path is added to the current claims register, `schema/state-schema.json`: that is
a schema change outside this row, and the file is deleted at row H.

# Architecture — `kernel/` § 5. Contracts

> Section file of [`kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../ARCHITECTURE.md), split from it whole on 2026-09-26 (TASK-488).
> Overflow convention: the root document's — split per § to `architecture/sections/§<N>-<topic>.md` — mirrored under `kernel/`.
> Cap: ≤ 600 lines, the module-document cap. A citation of `kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 5.x resolves here.

## §5. Contracts

### 5.1 The envelope, exit codes and error codes

Every command writes exactly one JSON object to stdout, with or without `--json`, and that
object is the whole answer. Anything a program must act on, warnings included, is a field
in it. On a refusal, stderr also carries one line, `kernel: <code>: <message>`, which
repeats `error` for a human. Every key is always present.

```json
{"ok": true, "surface": "1.0", "command": "item move", "effect": "written",
 "events": [57], "store_seq": 57, "warnings": [], "result": {"item": {"…": "…"}},
 "error": null}
```

`effect` is `written` (at least one event committed, or export files replaced),
`unchanged` (a write that found nothing to change and wrote no event), `dry_run` (the
transaction ran and was rolled back), `read`, or `refused`. `events` lists the seq of each
event this command committed, and is empty unless `effect` is `written`. `store_seq` is the
highest event seq visible to the command, after its commit. Reads carry it too, so a poller
can tell a stale read from a fresh one. On a refusal, `ok` is `false`, `result` is `null`,
and `error` is `{"code", "message", "details"}`. Exit codes: `0` success · `1` refused ·
`2` bad invocation · `3` internal fault (rolled back).

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | 2 | an unknown command, an undeclared flag or positional, a flag this command does not honour (`--dry-run` on a read), or a missing flag argument. Also a flag given twice, a flag given an empty value, `--input @` naming no file, an argument that is not valid UTF-8, `PERRY_STORE` or `PERRY_PROJECT` not valid UTF-8, and `PERRY_STORE` set but empty (§ 5.7) |
| `input_invalid` | 2 | `--input` is not exactly one JSON object, or a declared key has the wrong JSON type or a required one is missing. Not one JSON object includes a key given twice, bytes (stdin, an `@file`) that are not UTF-8, a lone surrogate in any string or key, a non-finite number, an integer outside −2⁶³ to 2⁶³−1, and nesting past 64 levels. A command's own input rule is this code too: a `state_root` that is empty, holds a backslash, a line break or a NUL, or is not a relative path inside the anchor, a relation naming both or neither of `to` and `from`, a field in both `set` and `unset`, a negative `limit` or `after_seq`, an `after` that is not an id, and a `where` or `count_by` field given without `type` or naming a `list` or `metric` field |
| `unknown_key` | 2 | the input carries a key the command does not declare, at any declared level. The legal set is named |
| `actor_invalid` | 2 | a write has no `actor`, the actor's `kind` is not `human` or `agent`, its `name` is empty, or an `agent` has no `session` |
